_doc: The Railroad Saloon, THE SILVER SPIKE (#1285; Sean 2026-11-26 on #1097: Payday Night's floor falls here, the dance floor upstairs over the bar; his picks in the session's chat the same day). Written by experiments/building_lab/railroad_saloon/make_spec.py: re-run it, never edit this by hand. Step 2 only: not built yet (the build is the next issue); fields marked NEW are what the builder may need adding.

identity.owner: a railroad contractor's ex-foreman who put it up in a fortnight in 1881 for the track gangs and never painted it
identity.trade: a cheap saloon: rotgut from the barrel, keg beer, a stove; a bare dance floor upstairs on paydays
identity.means: the cheapest drinking house in town: raw board-and-batten, a crude sign, one outside stair, nothing planed
identity.age_and_repair: 1 year: soot from the engines on the back, the floor's sawdust never swept out, a cracked window stuffed with a sack
clues: Lowry Bros. XXX tapped on the rack behind the bar (#1222)
the dance floor's boards worn pale in a ring where the reels go round
a track gang's tally chalked on the back door
a shovel and a lantern by the back door for the men from the pens

lot._doc: valley.json town.extras 'second_saloon' (centre [-42, -62], 12 x 9 m: x -48..-36, z -66.5..-57.5), between Back Street (z -54.25..-48.15) and the tracks, by the stock pens and the team track. The building on the lot's west half, its back wall on the lot's back line; 30 ft runs 0.14 m past the lot's front edge into the 3.25 m verge before Back Street (no walk on Back Street). Its east front corner is the origin. The outside stair stands on the lot's west edge (x -47.92); the 3.5 m yard east holds the empty kegs, the privy and the way round to the pens.

pad._doc: Probed (Python ValleyPlan terrain, this session): the ground rises 0.66 m front to back (world 2.18 at the front wall, 2.84 at the back) and falls 0.06 m west to east. The pad dug level at the front's ground (2.17) over the building, the stair and the yard, and 1.5 m on behind the back wall (off the lot, toward the tracks) so the back door opens onto the pad two steps down, the 0.7 m cut bank behind it. The build adds the lot's spec and pad to valley.json and re-bakes.

levels._doc: Low and cheap: the floor one plank step over the pad; 7 ft 6 in clear under the girder (8 ft 6 in to the joists), the dance floor at 3.245; 4 ft walls upstairs to the plate (benches under them) and a 10/12 roof open to its rafters, the ridge at 7.512.

frame._doc: A balloon frame, cheap (Bell 1858; Woodward 1865): rough-sawn full sizes, studs sill to plate, the dance floor's joists on a 1x6 ribbon let into the side walls' studs and on the one girder down the middle, on two posts. Sized by the USDA Wood Handbook for ponderosa pine (below and README.md).

foundation._doc: dry rubble piers and a stone sill course just to the pad: a cheap man's footing

joist._doc: the bar room's floor: 2x8 at 24 in between the ground girders (10 ft or less)

dance_joist._doc: 2x10 at 16 in over 11 ft 8 in, side wall to girder: 950 psi in the girder at Hatfield's 70 lb/ft2 dance load; the joists ~660 psi under the 1,000 psi the books allowed. Cut 12 mm short (end_gap) so a fallen bay doesn't jam.

floor_board._doc: wide 8 in boards, 1 in, square-edged (no tongue: the dust sifts through)

tall._doc: the side walls' studs 2x6: they take the roof's thrust over the 4 ft knee walls above the ribbon

post._doc: 6x6 rough posts on stone footings under the girder

beam._doc: THE GIRDER: one 6x12, jointed over its posts (three pieces)

rafters._doc: 2x6 at 24 in, 10/12, on the plates against a 1x8 ridge; a 2x6 collar on EVERY pair 8 ft over the dance floor (raised ties: the lamps hang from them); 1x8 roof boards, tar paper and battens; 12 in eaves.

truss._doc: unused (rafters above); kept for the builder's eave and board helpers, as the doctor's

girders._doc: under the bar room's floor, on stone piers, under the girder's posts

posts._doc: the girder's two 6x6 posts at 10 and 20 ft, each on a pier; its ends on wall posts in the front and back walls' studs

beams._doc: THE GIRDER THE BARON'S MEN SAW (#772): one line down the middle, jointed over its posts: beam/spine/0 (front bay), /1 (the middle bay, OVER THE BAR), /2 (back bay, under the piano). No brackets: they would catch the halves.

sabotage._doc: Payday Night: the middle bay's piece, cut at its middle. The story's cut is 9 of the 12 in sawn from below that morning (the pale kerf a lamp finds from the bar, S23), leaving 3 in: it holds the quiet afternoon at 3.7x and an ordinary night at 2.0x, and breaks at 1.2x when the payday reel stamps over it. In the game the event cuts it through (cut_member, a kerf) at its time; the bench measures the fall. Down come both sides' joists over the 10 ft bay, hinging on the side walls' ribbons: the east half onto the bar, the west half onto the tables.

floors._doc: THE DANCE FLOOR, the whole upstairs open to the roof, laid as three floors a bay each (RECIPE 'a balcony to be blown down': boards cut at the bay lines, or the fallen bay hangs on its neighbours' boards): 2x10s across the building broken over the girder, cut 12 mm short. The middle one, over the bar, is the one that falls.

walls._doc: To Back Street: the gable, the plank door west of the girder's line, a small window each side, two small windows over them upstairs; the sign board across the gable.

openings._doc: the wide plank door, off the girder's wall post (x 3.66)

walls._doc: To the tracks and the pens: the back door and the upstairs door over it (west of the girder's wall post), the landing outside between them; a small window high over the piano.

openings._doc: to the pens and the tracks, under the landing
the upstairs door off the landing: the only way in and out, THE JAM when the floor goes

walls._doc: The east side, to the yard: windows front and back of the bar (the racks stand between them), the same over them upstairs.
The west side, the outside stair's: two windows before the stair's foot, one small one under the eaves upstairs (the 4 ft knee wall).

stairs._doc: THE ONLY WAY UP: the outside stair up the west wall past the back corner to a landing behind the back wall and the upstairs door in the back gable. 17 risers of 7.5 in, 10 in treads, 3 ft 6 in wide, open on its outer side with a pole rail; three lines of posts under it. On Payday Night the two men go up it with a saw in the morning; Joe watches from it; the crowd jams it when the floor goes.
the back door's two steps down to the pad behind (the cut's bank 1.5 m back), under the landing
the front door's plank steps to the pad

balconies._doc: the outside stair's landing behind the back wall: from the stair's head (west, past the wall's end) to the door in the back gable; it roofs the back door under it. Three beams across it on posts, its joists along the wall over them (a stair's stringers on a beam, never a joist).

front._doc: a gable front, no false front: the crude sign board nailed across the gable between the door's head and the upper windows

rooms.use: the short bar down the east wall under the middle bay, barrels on racks behind it, the stove forward of the girder's front post, tables and benches west, spittoons, sawdust
benches round the walls, the piano and the band at the back wall, the door from the outside stair in the back gable, the reels in the middle

fixtures._doc: THE BAR: one 3 m built section (10 ft) down the east wall, exactly under the sawn bay (z 3.05-6.10); the customers west of it. UNDER THE CUT.
barrels on racks behind the bar against the east wall: Lowry Bros. XXX, Brandauer's, South Platte (#1222's rotgut)

furniture._doc: two rough tables west of the girder, under the falling west half
the front table by the window, clear of the fall

lamps._doc: #824's rules: smoky coal-oil lamps, few. Below: a reflector lamp on the yard wall by the bar's front end and one on the stair wall by the tables. Upstairs: two hung from the collars over the girder's posts (the dressing's `plan` batch, as saloon B's S1 hangs its lamps from joists) and one on the back wall by the piano.

dust._doc: dust sifts through the square-edged boards onto the bar; a fall under anyone moving upstairs (FloorDust); on Payday's last seconds, into the drinks

materials._doc: Step 4's: all raw. Outside the library's rough_pine_batten (approved R1 family), weathered; inside the same, unplaned; the floors FL1 worn hard. Never 'trial': true.

wear._why: a year of track gangs' boots, sawdust and spit; dents off until the judges like them (#901)

sources: USDA Forest Products Laboratory, Wood Handbook (FPL-GTR-282, 2021), ch. 5 Table 5-3a (ponderosa pine MOR, MOE), ch. 7 (strength ratios of knotty timber)
Hatfield, The American House Carpenter (1880): 70 lb/ft2 for a dance floor; Kidder, Building Construction and Superintendence (1895): ~1,000 psi working stress for pine
Bell, Carpentry Made Easy (1858); Woodward's National Architect (1869): balloon framing

dressing._doc: The plan's (README.md 'The crowd'): the prop lab places the rest by its recipe.

plan.use: carried up the outside stair that afternoon (S24): its back to the back wall, in the back bay (not the sawn one)

hung from the collar nearest the girder's back post
forward of the fall, its pipe up through the dance floor's front bay and the roof
